text:
Olivia: Hey team, customer (acct: acme-ux) reports a 3x spike in billed tokens for their /chat calls this week vs what they see in our realtime usage dashboard. dashboard shows ~120K tokens but invoice shows ~360K. Can someone explain?

Maya: sorry to hear that — can you paste a sample request id or timestamp? is this streaming or full-response? :thinking:

Olivia: Sample trace: request_id=req_0a3f, route=/v1/chat, model=rw-45b, timestamp=2026-11-09T14:22Z. They use streaming=true and set prefix_cache=enabled in client.

Devon: quick note: invoices count "metered_tokens" derived from our billing pipeline (served_tokens from runtime events aggregated by invoice window). Dashboards show per-route aggregated "client_reported" and "observed_requests" depending on telemetry ingestion. They can diverge if some runtime events are double-counted or if prefetching runs.

Olivia: Customer insists we billed for tokens that were never returned to them (prefetch/pinned-prompts). They say most responses are short, like 50-80 tokens, but invoice shows many large completions.

Rajat: I dug into runtime logs for req_0a3f. Here's the relevant excerpt: 
```
[2026-11-09T14:22:00Z] batcher: assigned to batch b202
[2026-11-09T14:22:00Z] prefetch: prefix_len=512 prefetch_hit=true src=kv-prefix
[2026-11-09T14:22:00Z] accounting: incrementing served_tokens += 512 (pending)
[2026-11-09T14:22:01Z] kv-lookup: cache_hit=true matched_prefix_len=512
[2026-11-09T14:22:01Z] response: streamed_chunks=3 final_tokens=78
[2026-11-09T14:22:01Z] accounting: finalized served_tokens += 78
```
Rajat: Looks like the early accounting increment counts the prefetched prefix (512) before we confirm cache_hit. If the prefix is served from cache it should not be billed as newly generated tokens, but our pipeline currently counts the prefetch increment in served_tokens and then also finalizes with final_tokens, causing an overcount when the prefetch was from cache.

Maya: ah ok — customer is using continuous batching + prefix caching heavily. So background prefetch requests for cold-start heuristics are being recorded as served.

Devon: that matches invoice timing: spikes at 14:22 and recurring every ~5m (prefetch interval). Billing window aggregated those early increments. Dashboard pipelines filter out events flagged cache_hit=true because they derive usage from post-kv-lookup metrics, which is why dashboard shows the lower number.

Olivia: Can we reproduce and quantify how many tokens get double-counted? Customer wants a credit if confirmed.

Rajat: Repro steps I used locally (small script):
```
# simulate continuous prefetch + streaming
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -d '{"model":"rw-45b","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"<prefill 512 tokens>"},{"role":"user","content":"short"}],"stream":true,"prefix_cache":true}'
```
Then watch runtime logs for prefetch accounting events. With telemetry enabled I reproduced ~480 extra served_tokens per call when prefix_cache prefetch ran and resolved to cache_hit.

Maya: thanks. Next steps?

Devon: short-term remediation: we can run a one-off recalculation for affected invoice window that subtracts prefetch_increments where a subsequent kv-lookup had cache_hit=true and the event attribution is to the same request_id. I'll open a billing-adjustment ticket if eng confirms logic.

Rajat: long-term fix: move the accounting event to after kv-lookup resolution OR add a compensating event when prefetch resolves to cache_hit. Minimal patch: emit prefetch_mark with temporary counter and finalize only the delta between generated tokens and cached_prefix_len. I'll open PR to change accounting ordering in the batcher: proposed change is to stop writing served_tokens at prefetch stage, instead write prefetch_pending_tokens and reconcile after kv response.

Olivia: Customer asked for ETA on credit and the code fix.

Devon: I'll request a provisional credit for acme-ux for the overage from 2026-11-09T00:00 to 2026-11-10T00:00 and flag for review. Need confirmation of total overcount first.

Rajat: I can run a job to reprocess runtime events for that window and produce an "adjusted_served_tokens" metric. Expect ~+/- 5% runtime; job ETA 24 hours.

Maya: I'll keep customer updated. tagging @Devon for billing action and @Rajat for the repro artifacts.

Devon: opened billing ticket #BILL-8642 and added provisional credit note.

billing-bot: Ticket BILL-8642 created by Devon. Status: triaged.

Olivia: Thanks all. Customer asked for a short explanation we can send: can someone draft a 2-line summary we can paste?

Rajat: Draft: "We found a bug in runtime accounting where prefetch token increments were recorded before the KV cache resolution. When a prefix is served entirely from cache, those prefetch increments were not removed, leading to over-reporting of served tokens. We're reprocessing the affected window and will issue a credit for confirmed overage."

Maya: perfect. I'll send that to the customer and include the provisional credit note.

Olivia: Closing here once Devon confirms credit issued and Rajat posts repro artifacts. Thanks :white_check_mark:
